waves.name: Reader job against the legacy file
waves.rationale: READJOB reads SPARQ.TEST.MASTER and writes nothing another job uses, so the port can be checked against files the legacy writer already produced. It is the consumer side of the one contract in the tree, so porting it first forces the 80 byte record and the 15 byte layout to be written down before anything that produces them changes. Rollback is to run the legacy PGMR step again. No computed calls, no cycle.
waves.unblocks: Wave 2. The layout and record length pinned here are the specification the new writer must meet.

waves.name: Writer job and the single layout
waves.rationale: WRITEJOB creates the dataset READJOB reads, so it is the producer side of the contract. It moves after the reader because the reader harness from wave 1 is what proves the new output is byte-compatible. Confidence is medium, not high: the program writes its record without setting any field, so the legacy behavior has to come from a captured output file, not from the source. The nightly cycle is the named must-not-break item and the scheduler that orders it is not in the tree.
waves.unblocks: Retiring the second copybook. Once the new writer matches the pinned layout, LAYOUTX and LAYOUTY can become one definition.
